solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Good streak ergo good will

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
to streak is to race along at speed

explanation.surface: A vein of goodness, and therefore kindly intentions.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace in the sense of favour or kindness freely shown is a near synonym of benevolence.

clue.text: School kid's fun amongst locals

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
to kid someone is to tease or mock them; the 's is read as 'is', joining the pieces

explanation.surface: Playground japes among the children of a neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amongst locals' marks the answer as a dialect word, so it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammock is a dialect word for a frolic or bit of horseplay, so it is merriment in regional speech.

clue.text: Bucolic god with prefix meaning primitive set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god
ur- is the prefix meaning original or primitive, as in Urtext

explanation.surface: A pastoral deity of primeval origin, raised on a pedestal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic and the answer are both adjectives describing the countryside and farming life.

clue.text: A dreadful experience over too much drink

parts.note: taken as written
a mare, short for nightmare, is a horrible experience

indicators.note: over suggests turning something upside down, so in a down entry the letters flip

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: An evening of overindulgence that ends in an awful ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Go round second-rate store passing over hard PC's part? (12, two words)

indicators.note: to pass over something is to skip it, leaving it out of the word

parts.note: a circuit is a go round, a lap
B grade is second rate
a hoard is a store
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Instructions for a shopper: walk around a cheap shop but skip the difficult stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of the store word is dropped. The question mark admits the definition is an example: a computer is only one place to find one.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer contains printed boards carrying its electronic components, so one is a component of a personal computer.

clue.text: Jangle in the old way as Queen related

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', that is, as
R for Regina, the Latin for queen
rel. is the dictionary abbreviation for related

explanation.surface: A royal who once rang bells harshly, or so the story is told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jangle' wants to be the noise of bells, but its archaic sense is to bicker; 'in the old way' flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Jangle once meant to wrangle or dispute noisily, which is exactly what a quarrel is.

clue.text: Share quarterly round after ripping off its leader

indicators.note: tearing off the leader removes the opening letter of the word just before

parts.note: qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for quarterly
a rota is a round of duties taken in turn

explanation.surface: A shareholder's quarterly dividend paid out after the chairman is ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is an allotted portion, the share assigned to each party.

clue.text: Half of fake old Omani bread's to do with the Dutch

indicators.note: half of a word means only two of its four letters are kept, here the back pair

parts.note: faux means fake; its second half is kept
O is the abbreviation for old
bread is slang for money, and the rial is the currency of Oman

explanation.surface: Half a counterfeit loaf from Oman turns out to be Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife (from 'my old Dutch'), so the answer means relating to a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorial means pertaining to a wife, and a man's Dutch is his wife in Cockney usage.

clue.text: Drawing, say, direct from what's plastered over walls?

parts.note: drawing is an example of art
ex means sold direct from, as in ex works

explanation.surface: A sketch taken straight from graffiti daubed over the town walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade name is in Chambers; the question mark admits it is more often found on ceilings.
explanation.definitionFit: Artex is a textured plaster-like coating applied to interior walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Save theatre I bail out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rescue plan for a failing playhouse: I pay to get it out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehabilitate something is to restore and redeem it, much as one saves a reputation or a building.

clue.text: And in France fiddle heading off the cause of whiteness?

indicators.note: with its heading off, the instrument loses its first letter

parts.note: et is French for and
a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: A French violinist whose bow is lost, wondering why he has gone pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiolin is the pigment found in etiolated plants, those blanched by growing without light, hence a cause of pallor.

clue.text: Before dropping in bone up on site of Herculean triumph

indicators.note: in a down entry, a letter dropping drops lower down the column, leaving its old place

parts.note: to bone up is to study, to learn
a. stands for ante, Latin for before

explanation.surface: Revise before your exam on where Hercules won a famous victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in the study word falls to the bottom of the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerna in Greek legend is the marsh where Hercules slew the many-headed Hydra, one of his twelve labours.

clue.text: D'Estaing's on the best of terms with mistress hugging plummy wife (7, two words)

definitions.text: D'Estaing's on the best of terms

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap around it, holding it inside

parts.note: amie is French for a female friend or mistress
U means upper class, and a plummy voice is a posh one
ux. is the abbreviation for uxor, Latin for wife

explanation.surface: A French president on cosy terms with both his mistress and his posh wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Giscard d'Estaing was a French president, so his name signals a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Au mieux is French for on the best of terms, especially with a hint of intimacy.

clue.text: Income received yearly is split by Earl

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend: torn, split
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An earl's annual income is divided in a family dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Rente is an annual return or annuity, especially from French government stock.

clue.text: Ferret locks an underground place of intake (8, two words)

parts.note: to ferret about is to root around
locks are hair

explanation.surface: A ferret's fur and a burrow where it feeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Root hairs are fine outgrowths on plant roots that absorb water and nutrients from the soil.

clue.text: Early descent — defile it with debate

parts.note: to defile is to march in file; 'it' becomes the old contraction 't, as in march't
to reason is to argue or debate

explanation.surface: An old genealogy has been corrupted, and the matter is argued.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'defile' as spoil leads nowhere; it is the military sense. A descent here is a raid, and march-treason was the offence of raiding across a border in peacetime.
explanation.definitionFit: March-treason was the historical crime of raiding a neighbouring country from the marches, an unlawful incursion of former times.

clue.text: Acidic solution round part of gut I must draw off

indicators.note: drawing off the single letter named removes it from the gut part

parts.note: O is round in shape
the ileum is the final section of the small intestine

explanation.surface: A surgeon describing an acid wash used before draining part of the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleum is fuming sulphuric acid, sulphur trioxide dissolved in the concentrated acid.

clue.text: Plant label iPad's assistant turned up (8, two words)

parts.note: to flag is to mark or label

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Siri is Apple's voice assistant

explanation.surface: Someone tagging their tablet's voice helper when it finally appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag iris is a waterside iris, a flowering species found by ponds.

clue.text: Bright flier turned it into dance

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside the other word

parts.note: the conga is a line dance

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the little word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: A brightly dressed pilot spun round and joined a party dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotingas are brilliantly plumaged tropical American birds, so one is a colourful bird.

clue.text: Fodder like oca, in some other way

indicators.note: done in another way means arranged differently, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the fodder; oca is an Andean tuber

explanation.surface: Cattle feed rather like an Andean root crop, but prepared differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcake is pressed seed residue from oil extraction, fed to livestock as cattle feed.

clue.text: Recover from urge to verify to some extent (7, two words)

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so the answer sits within a stretch of the clue

parts.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: Getting better after an insistent need to check everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over an illness or setback is to recuperate from it.

clue.text: Spots one thousand bones

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the ilia are the hip bones, plural of ilium

explanation.surface: Someone sees a thousand bones lying about.
explanation.definitionFit: Milia are tiny white cysts on the skin, small blemishes plural like the clue's noun.

clue.text: Barking mad one with a mild swelling

indicators.note: barking means crazy, and crazy letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lunatic with a minor lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'Barking' (slang for crazy) does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: An adenoma is a benign tumour of glandular tissue, so a non-cancerous growth.

clue.text: Bowler sets her sights on this equipment to go right away

definitions.text: Bowler sets her sights on this

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right is sent off from the word

parts.note: kit is equipment
a go is a try

explanation.surface: A bowler eyes new gear and wants to be off at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is not a cricketer: in lawn bowls, players aim at the small white jack, also called the kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: In bowls the kitty is the jack, the small target ball every player aims at.

clue.text: Antelope flourished within enchanted place

indicators.note: within places the abbreviation inside the animal word

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope
fl. is the abbreviation for floruit, Latin for flourished

explanation.surface: An antelope thriving in a magical realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfland is fairyland, the magical home of elves.

clue.text: Forest greenery covering second kilometre, or so, in the taiga

definitions.text: kilometre, or so, in the taiga

indicators.note: to cover something is to enclose it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: vert is the old forest-law term for green vegetation in a forest
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Green woodland stretching a kilometre across the Siberian forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The taiga is the Russian forest belt, hinting at a Russian unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A verst is an old Russian measure of distance, about 1.07 km, so roughly a kilometre.

clue.text: Helping head getting to grips with learner

indicators.note: gripping something holds it inside, so one piece encloses the letter

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
L is the abbreviation for a learner driver

explanation.surface: A head teacher assisting a pupil who is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb but is the noun: a serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate, or plateful, is a portion of food, a serving.

clue.text: Put up chauffeur for Indian importing good smokes?

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up makes it read from the bottom upward
to import is to bring inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a sice or syce in India is a groom or attendant, sometimes a driver
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An Indian driver brings in some decent cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Anglo-Indian word for a groom later came to cover a chauffeur too. The question mark admits these are not real smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: E-cigs are electronic cigarettes, vaped rather than lit, so arguably smokes.

clue.text: For example, dosh mostly backing early form of press

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse
mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
gilt is slang for money, as dosh is

explanation.surface: Cash supporting an early printing press, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' wants to be a printing press; it is a verb. Ligge is an obsolete spelling found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligge is an archaic verb form, glossed by the setter as an old word for bearing or pressing down.

clue.text: Great getting round SOE ground — progress now discontinued

indicators.note: getting round something means encircling it

parts.note: gt is the abbreviation for great

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written; the wartime Special Operations Executive

explanation.surface: A great wartime spy network gets to work on the ground, though its advance is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now discontinued' marks an archaic verb form, the old second person singular.
explanation.definitionFit: Goest is the old 'thou' form of go, and to go is to progress, a form no longer used.

clue.text: English as coded by sparks ain't cool surprisingly for Asdic? (12, two words)

parts.note: Echo is the radio alphabet's word for E, and a sparks is a radio operator

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio operator complains that coding English is not much fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Asdic was the British name for early submarine-detecting sonar.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic finds objects by bouncing sound pulses off them, which is the principle of echolocation; the question mark admits it is an example.

clue.text: Two charges on shield without any power is a thing seldom seen (8, two words)

indicators.note: without any power means every letter standing for power is removed

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, and there are two
a pavis is a large medieval shield
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Heraldry: a shield with two emblems but no symbol of authority is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' and 'shield' paint heraldry, but the charges are criminal raps. All three Ps go.
explanation.definitionFit: Rara avis, Latin for rare bird, describes an exceptional person or thing that is rarely encountered.

clue.text: Run piercing spoof to split from pack

indicators.note: piercing means going into, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a skit is a spoof or parody
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A parody of a break-away runner leaving the field behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The pack is a pack of hounds: a hound skirts when it cuts corners away from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In hunting, a hound that skirts runs wide of the line, leaving the rest of the pack.

clue.text: Wanting aspiration he caught his male braggadocio

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and aspiration is the breathy sound written with a single letter, so that letter goes wherever it appears

parts.note: taken as written
got means caught
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: An unambitious man who caught his own boastful male rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspiration is the breathy H sound, so both Hs drop out.
explanation.definitionFit: Braggadocio is empty boasting, which springs from an inflated self-regard, conceit.

clue.text: Support craft apt to list with opening of sail

parts.note: a ship that is tender heels over easily

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of sail

explanation.surface: A rescue boat liable to keel over the moment a sail is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks like a verb, but support craft are the boats that service larger ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenders are small vessels ferrying supplies and people to larger ships, auxiliary boats.

clue.text: Match versus Spain gaining reduced support

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for versus
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a stay is a support or brace

explanation.surface: A football fixture against Spain where the team gains thinner backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' wants to be a sporting fixture; it is the thing you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesta is a short wax friction match for lighting, named after the Roman goddess of the hearth.
